title: What If Niagara Falls Suddenly Ran Dry?

scenes.text: What if Niagara Falls ran dry? It has happened. Twice.
In March eighteen forty-eight, ice jammed the river's mouth, and the flow stopped for about thirty hours.
People walked out onto the exposed riverbed. Some found old muskets and bayonets from the War of eighteen twelve.
In nineteen sixty-nine, engineers did it on purpose. They built a six hundred foot dam of twenty-eight thousand tons of rock.
For five months, one of the world's most famous waterfalls was a trickle, so geologists could study the cliff.
When the dam came down, the water roared back that same night. The falls had been switched off, and nobody noticed it missing.

description:
What if Niagara Falls ran dry?
It already has: ice stopped the river for about thirty hours in 1848, and engineers shut off the American Falls for five months in 1969.
What should we run through next?
